# Resource: stripe_setup_intent

Collects a customer's payment method for later use. Set `status` to `canceled` to cancel the intent; one that already succeeded cannot be canceled. Confirming an intent is not a resource: confirm it with its `client_secret` from your front end, or from your server with Stripe's API, and `status` reports what happened. The resource has no `confirm` or `mandate_data` argument, and Stripe refuses `payment_method_options.card.three_d_secure` on an intent that is not being confirmed. Setting `payment_method` moves the intent to `requires_confirmation`. `usage` and `on_behalf_of` cannot change after creation, and neither can the other arguments that only a create takes, so changing one fails the plan. The `client_secret` is sensitive and stays in the state.

~> Stripe cannot delete a setup intent; set `status` to `canceled` to cancel one. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the setup intent, fail at plan time. To stop managing a setup intent, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_customer" "acme" {
  email = "billing@acme.example"
}

# Hand the client secret to your front end, which collects and confirms the payment method.
resource "stripe_setup_intent" "card" {
  customer = stripe_customer.acme.id
  usage    = "off_session"

  automatic_payment_methods = {
    enabled         = true
    allow_redirects = "never"
  }
}

output "client_secret" {
  value     = stripe_setup_intent.card.client_secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are optional:

* `allowed_payment_method_types` - (Optional) The list of payment method types to allow for this SetupIntent. Stripe will only use methods in this list when determining the payment methods to offer. A list of valid payment method types can be found [here](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/object#payment_method_object-type). Default: none.
* `attach_to_self` - (Optional) If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the in-context Stripe Account. It can only be used for this Stripe Account’s own money movement flows like InboundTransfer and OutboundTransfers. It cannot be set to true when setting up a PaymentMethod for a Customer, and defaults to false when attaching a PaymentMethod to a Customer. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Stripe refused it on a US account on update: "The parameter attach_to_self has already been set on this SetupIntent and cannot be updated.". Default: none. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `automatic_payment_methods` - (Optional) When you enable this parameter, this SetupIntent accepts payment methods that you enable in the Dashboard and that are compatible with its other parameters. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`automatic_payment_methods`](#automatic_payment_methods) below.
* `confirmation_token` - (Optional) ID of the ConfirmationToken used to confirm this SetupIntent. If the provided ConfirmationToken contains properties that are also being provided in this request, such as `payment_method`, then the values in this request will take precedence. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Stripe refused it on a US account on create: "No such confirmationtoken: 'ctoken_...'".
* `customer` - (Optional) ID of the Customer this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists. If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Customer on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this SetupIntent. Default: none.
* `customer_account` - (Optional) ID of the Account this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists. If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Account on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Accounts cannot be used with this SetupIntent. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Stripe refused it on a US account on create and update: "The supplied ID is not a valid Customer. V2 Accounts must be configured as Customers before they can be used in the Customers API.". Default: none.
* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users. Default: none.
* `excluded_payment_method_types` - (Optional) The list of payment method types to exclude from use with this SetupIntent. Default: none.
* `flow_directions` - (Optional) Indicates the directions of money movement for which this payment method is intended to be used. Include `inbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the origin to pull funds from. Include `outbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the destination to send funds to. You can include both if you intend to use the payment method for both purposes. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`. Default (Stripe): `{}`.
* `on_behalf_of` - (Optional) The Stripe account ID created for this SetupIntent. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Default: none.
* `payment_method` - (Optional) ID of the payment method (a PaymentMethod, Card, or saved Source object) to attach to this SetupIntent. Default (Stripe): none, or the method Stripe makes from `payment_method_data`, which this attribute does not hold.
* `payment_method_configuration` - (Optional) The ID of the [payment method configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_method_configurations) to use with this SetupIntent. Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `payment_method_data` - (Optional) When included, this hash creates a PaymentMethod that is set as the [`payment_method`](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/object#setup_intent_object-payment_method) value in the SetupIntent. See [`payment_method_data`](#payment_method_data) below.
* `payment_method_options` - (Optional) Payment method-specific configuration for this SetupIntent. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_method_options`](#payment_method_options) below.
* `single_use` - (Optional) If you populate this hash, this SetupIntent generates a `single_use` mandate after successful completion. Single-use mandates are only valid for the following payment methods: `acss_debit`, `alipay`, `au_becs_debit`, `bacs_debit`, `bancontact`, `boleto`, `ideal`, `link`, `sepa_debit`, and `us_bank_account`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration. See [`single_use`](#single_use) below.
* `status` - (Optional) [Status](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/intents#intent-statuses) of this SetupIntent, one of `requires_payment_method`, `requires_confirmation`, `requires_action`, `processing`, `canceled`, or `succeeded`. Possible values: `canceled`. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.
* `usage` - (Optional) Indicates how the payment method is intended to be used in the future. If not provided, this value defaults to `off_session`. Possible values: `off_session`, `on_session`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Default (Stripe): `off_session`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="automatic_payment_methods"></a>
### `automatic_payment_methods`

The `automatic_payment_methods` attribute supports:

* `allow_redirects` - (Optional) Controls whether this SetupIntent will accept redirect-based payment methods. Redirect-based payment methods may require your customer to be redirected to a payment method's app or site for authentication or additional steps. To [confirm](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/confirm) this SetupIntent, you may be required to provide a `return_url` to redirect customers back to your site after they authenticate or complete the setup. Possible values: `always`, `never`. Default (Stripe): `always`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `enabled` - (Required) Automatically calculates compatible payment methods

<a id="payment_method_options.klarna"></a>
### `payment_method_options.klarna`

The `payment_method_options.klarna` attribute supports:

* `currency` - (Optional) The currency of the setup intent. Three letter ISO currency code. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `on_demand` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration. See [`payment_method_options.klarna.on_demand`](#payment_method_options.klarna.on_demand) below.
* `preferred_locale` - (Optional) Preferred locale of the Klarna checkout page that the customer is redirected to. Possible values: `cs-CZ`, `da-DK`, `de-AT`, `de-CH`, `de-DE`, `el-GR`, `en-AT`, `en-AU`, `en-BE`, `en-CA`, `en-CH`, `en-CZ`, `en-DE`, `en-DK`, `en-ES`, `en-FI`, `en-FR`, `en-GB`, `en-GR`, `en-IE`, `en-IT`, `en-NL`, `en-NO`, `en-NZ`, `en-PL`, `en-PT`, `en-RO`, `en-SE`, `en-US`, `es-ES`, `es-US`, `fi-FI`, `fr-BE`, `fr-CA`, `fr-CH`, `fr-FR`, `it-CH`, `it-IT`, `nb-NO`, `nl-BE`, `nl-NL`, `pl-PL`, `pt-PT`, `ro-RO`, `sv-FI`, `sv-SE`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `subscriptions` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration. See [`payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions`](#payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions) below.

<a id="payment_method_options.klarna.on_demand"></a>
### `payment_method_options.klarna.on_demand`

The `payment_method_options.klarna.on_demand` attribute supports:

* `average_amount` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.
* `maximum_amount` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.
* `minimum_amount` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.
* `purchase_interval` - (Optional) Possible values: `day`, `month`, `week`, `year`. Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.
* `purchase_interval_count` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.

<a id="payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions"></a>
### `payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions`

The `payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `interval` - (Required) Possible values: `day`, `month`, `week`, `year`. Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.
* `interval_count` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.
* `name` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.
* `next_billing` - (Required) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration. See [`payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions.next_billing`](#payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions.next_billing) below.
* `reference` - (Required) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.

<a id="payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions.next_billing"></a>
### `payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions.next_billing`

The `payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions.next_billing` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Required) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.
* `date` - (Required) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.

<a id="payment_method_options.pix"></a>
### `payment_method_options.pix`

The `payment_method_options.pix` attribute supports:

* `mandate_options` - (Optional) Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options`](#payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options) below.

<a id="payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options"></a>
### `payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options`

The `payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) Amount to be charged for future payments. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `amount_includes_iof` - (Optional) Determines if the amount includes the IOF tax. Possible values: `always`, `never`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `amount_type` - (Optional) Type of amount. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `currency` - (Optional) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `end_date` - (Optional) Date when the mandate expires and no further payments will be charged, in `YYYY-MM-DD`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `payment_schedule` - (Optional) Schedule at which the future payments will be charged. Possible values: `halfyearly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `weekly`, `yearly`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `reference` - (Optional) Subscription name displayed to buyers in their bank app. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `start_date` - (Optional) Start date of the mandate, in `YYYY-MM-DD`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.sepa_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_options.sepa_debit`

The `payment_method_options.sepa_debit` attribute supports:

* `mandate_options` - (Optional) Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_method_options.sepa_debit.mandate_options`](#payment_method_options.sepa_debit.mandate_options) below.

<a id="payment_method_options.sepa_debit.mandate_options"></a>
### `payment_method_options.sepa_debit.mandate_options`

The `payment_method_options.sepa_debit.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `reference_prefix` - (Optional) Prefix used to generate the Mandate reference. Must be at most 12 characters long. Must consist of only uppercase letters, numbers, spaces, or the following special characters: '/', '_', '-', '&', '.'. Cannot begin with 'STRIPE'. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.upi"></a>
### `payment_method_options.upi`

The `payment_method_options.upi` attribute supports:

* `mandate_options` - (Optional) Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options`](#payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options) below.
* `setup_future_usage` - (Optional) Possible values: `none`, `off_session`, `on_session`. Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.

<a id="payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options"></a>
### `payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options`

The `payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) Amount to be charged for future payments. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `amount_type` - (Optional) One of `fixed` or `maximum`. If `fixed`, the `amount` param refers to the exact amount to be charged in future payments. If `maximum`, the amount charged can be up to the value passed for the `amount` param. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `description` - (Optional) A description of the mandate or subscription that is meant to be displayed to the customer. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `end_date` - (Optional) End date of the mandate or subscription. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.us_bank_account"></a>
### `payment_method_options.us_bank_account`

The `payment_method_options.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `financial_connections` - (Optional) Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections`](#payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections) below.
* `mandate_options` - (Optional) Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_method_options.us_bank_account.mandate_options`](#payment_method_options.us_bank_account.mandate_options) below.
* `networks` - (Optional) See [`payment_method_options.us_bank_account.networks`](#payment_method_options.us_bank_account.networks) below.
* `verification_method` - (Optional) Bank account verification method. The default value is `automatic`. Possible values: `automatic`, `instant`, `microdeposits`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections"></a>
### `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections`

The `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections` attribute supports:

* `filters` - (Optional) Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections.filters`](#payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections.filters) below.
* `permissions` - (Optional) The list of permissions to request. The `payment_method` permission must be included. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `prefetch` - (Optional) Data features requested to be retrieved upon account creation. Stripe refused it on a US account on create and update: "You do not have the required permissions to prefetch.". Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `return_url` - (Optional) For webview integrations only. Upon completing OAuth login in the native browser, the user will be redirected to this URL to return to your app. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections.filters"></a>
### `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections.filters`

The `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections.filters` attribute supports:

* `account_subcategories` - (Optional) The account subcategories to use to filter for possible accounts to link. Valid subcategories are `checking` and `savings`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.us_bank_account.mandate_options"></a>
### `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.mandate_options`

The `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `collection_method` - (Optional) Mandate collection method Possible values: `paper`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.us_bank_account.networks"></a>
### `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.networks`

The `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.networks` attribute supports:

* `requested` - (Optional) Stripe refused it on a US account on create and update: "To use the `us_domestic_wire` network, the PaymentMethod must include billing address information. Please update the PaymentMethod or include the following missing field(s) in your payment method data under `billing_details[address]` and try again: line1, city, state, postal_code, country".

<a id="single_use"></a>
### `single_use`

The `single_use` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Required) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.
* `currency` - (Required) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `application` - ID of the Connect application that created the SetupIntent.
* `cancellation_reason` - Reason for cancellation of this SetupIntent, one of `abandoned`, `requested_by_customer`, or `duplicate`. Possible values: `abandoned`, `duplicate`, `requested_by_customer`.
* `client_secret` - (Sensitive) The client secret of this SetupIntent. Used for client-side retrieval using a publishable key. The client secret can be used to complete payment setup from your frontend. It should not be stored, logged, or exposed to anyone other than the customer. Make sure that you have TLS enabled on any page that includes the client secret.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `last_setup_error` - The error encountered in the previous SetupIntent confirmation. See [`last_setup_error`](#last_setup_error) below.
* `latest_attempt` - The most recent SetupAttempt for this SetupIntent.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `managed_payments` - See [`managed_payments`](#managed_payments) below.
* `mandate` - ID of the multi use Mandate generated by the SetupIntent.
* `next_action` - If present, this property tells you what actions you need to take in order for your customer to continue payment setup. See [`next_action`](#next_action) below.
* `payment_method_configuration_details` - Information about the [payment method configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_method_configurations) used for this Setup Intent. See [`payment_method_configuration_details`](#payment_method_configuration_details) below.
* `payment_method_types` - The list of payment method types (e.g. card) that this SetupIntent is allowed to set up. A list of valid payment method types can be found [here](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/object#payment_method_object-type).
* `single_use_mandate` - ID of the single_use Mandate generated by the SetupIntent.

<a id="last_setup_error"></a>
### `last_setup_error`

The `last_setup_error` attribute supports:

* `advice_code` - For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a short string indicating [how to proceed with an error](https://docs.stripe.com/declines/card#retrying-issuer-declines) if they provide one.
* `charge` - For card errors, the ID of the failed charge.
* `code` - For some errors that could be handled programmatically, a short string indicating the [error code](https://docs.stripe.com/error-codes) reported.
* `decline_code` - For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a short string indicating the [card issuer's reason for the decline](https://docs.stripe.com/declines#issuer-declines) if they provide one.
* `doc_url` - A URL to more information about the [error code](https://docs.stripe.com/error-codes) reported.
* `message` - A human-readable message providing more details about the error. For card errors, these messages can be shown to your users.
* `network_advice_code` - For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a 2 digit code which indicates the advice given to merchant by the card network on how to proceed with an error.
* `network_decline_code` - For payments declined by the network, an alphanumeric code which indicates the reason the payment failed.
* `param` - If the error is parameter-specific, the parameter related to the error. For example, you can use this to display a message near the correct form field.
* `payment_method` - PaymentMethod objects represent your customer's payment instruments. You can use them with [PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents) to collect payments or save them to Customer objects to store instrument details for future payments. Related guides: [Payment Methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods) and [More Payment Scenarios](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/more-payment-scenarios). See [`last_setup_error.payment_method`](#last_setup_error.payment_method) below.
* `payment_method_type` - If the error is specific to the type of payment method, the payment method type that had a problem. This field is only populated for invoice-related errors.
* `request_log_url` - A URL to the request log entry in your dashboard.
* `type` - The type of error returned. One of `api_error`, `card_error`, `idempotency_error`, or `invalid_request_error` Possible values: `api_error`, `card_error`, `idempotency_error`, `invalid_request_error`.

<a id="last_setup_error.payment_method"></a>
### `last_setup_error.payment_method`

The `last_setup_error.payment_method` attribute holds a customer payment method, with the attributes of the [`stripe_customer_payment_method`](../data-sources/customer_payment_method) data source and `object`, the name of its type.

<a id="managed_payments"></a>
### `managed_payments`

The `managed_payments` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - Set to `true` to enable [Managed Payments](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments), Stripe's merchant of record solution, for this session.

<a id="next_action"></a>
### `next_action`

The `next_action` attribute supports:

* `cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code` - See [`next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code`](#next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code) below.
* `pix_display_qr_code` - See [`next_action.pix_display_qr_code`](#next_action.pix_display_qr_code) below.
* `redirect_to_url` - See [`next_action.redirect_to_url`](#next_action.redirect_to_url) below.
* `type` - Type of the next action to perform. Refer to the other child attributes under `next_action` for available values. Examples include: `redirect_to_url`, `use_stripe_sdk`, `alipay_handle_redirect`, `oxxo_display_details`, or `verify_with_microdeposits`.
* `upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code` - See [`next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code`](#next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code) below.
* `verify_with_microdeposits` - See [`next_action.verify_with_microdeposits`](#next_action.verify_with_microdeposits) below.

<a id="next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code"></a>
### `next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code`

The `next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code` attribute supports:

* `hosted_instructions_url` - The URL to the hosted Cash App Pay instructions page, which allows customers to view the QR code, and supports QR code refreshing on expiration.
* `mobile_auth_url` - The url for mobile redirect based auth
* `qr_code` - See [`next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code`](#next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code) below.

<a id="next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code"></a>
### `next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code`

The `next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code` attribute supports:

* `expires_at` - The date (unix timestamp) when the QR code expires.
* `image_url_png` - The image_url_png string used to render QR code
* `image_url_svg` - The image_url_svg string used to render QR code

<a id="next_action.pix_display_qr_code"></a>
### `next_action.pix_display_qr_code`

The `next_action.pix_display_qr_code` attribute supports:

* `data` - The raw data string used to generate QR code, it should be used together with QR code library.
* `expires_at` - The date (unix timestamp) when the PIX expires.
* `hosted_instructions_url` - The URL to the hosted pix instructions page, which allows customers to view the pix QR code.
* `image_url_png` - The image_url_png string used to render png QR code
* `image_url_svg` - The image_url_svg string used to render svg QR code

<a id="next_action.redirect_to_url"></a>
### `next_action.redirect_to_url`

The `next_action.redirect_to_url` attribute supports:

* `return_url` - If the customer does not exit their browser while authenticating, they will be redirected to this specified URL after completion.
* `url` - The URL you must redirect your customer to in order to authenticate.

<a id="next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code"></a>
### `next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code`

The `next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code` attribute supports:

* `hosted_instructions_url` - The URL to the hosted UPI instructions page, which allows customers to view the QR code.
* `qr_code` - See [`next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code`](#next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code) below.

<a id="next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code"></a>
### `next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code`

The `next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code` attribute supports:

* `expires_at` - The date (unix timestamp) when the QR code expires.
* `image_url_png` - The image_url_png string used to render QR code
* `image_url_svg` - The image_url_svg string used to render QR code

<a id="next_action.verify_with_microdeposits"></a>
### `next_action.verify_with_microdeposits`

The `next_action.verify_with_microdeposits` attribute supports:

* `arrival_date` - The timestamp when the microdeposits are expected to land.
* `hosted_verification_url` - The URL for the hosted verification page, which allows customers to verify their bank account.
* `microdeposit_type` - The type of the microdeposit sent to the customer. Used to distinguish between different verification methods. Possible values: `amounts`, `descriptor_code`.

<a id="payment_method_configuration_details"></a>
### `payment_method_configuration_details`

The `payment_method_configuration_details` attribute supports:

* `id` - ID of the payment method configuration used.
* `parent` - ID of the parent payment method configuration used.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a setup intent whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_setup_intent.card

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_setup_intent.card
```

The setup intent stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a setup intent using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_setup_intent.card
  id = "seti_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_setup_intent.card
  identity = {
    id = "seti_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the setup intent.

Using `terraform import`, import a setup intent using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_setup_intent.card seti_123
```

~> Stripe does not return `payment_method_configuration`, `payment_method_data`, `payment_method_options.card`, `payment_method_options.klarna.on_demand`, `payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions`, `payment_method_options.upi.setup_future_usage`, `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.networks`, `confirmation_token` or `single_use`, so an imported setup intent has them null: a configuration that sets `payment_method_configuration`, `payment_method_data`, `payment_method_options.card`, `payment_method_options.klarna.on_demand`, `payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions`, `payment_method_options.upi.setup_future_usage` or `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.networks` plans an update after the import, and one that sets `confirmation_token` or `single_use` plans a replacement.
